title: 2026 BMW F450 GS Trophy Review - Auto Trader NZ
content: If you don’t already know, the ‘GS’ suffix that BMW Motorrad attaches to its adventure models stands for ‘Gelände Strasse’, roughly ‘off-road/on-road’ in German. It highlights the compromise all adventure bike manufacturers must make when designing a new model. Do they make it more rideable in ‘Gelände’ riding scenarios, or do they retain more of its performance during ‘Strasse’ applications? For, as any ute owner who has fitted big mud-slinging treads already knows, upping drivability for the times when the vehicle is off-road always compromises refinement and the on-road dynamics when back in the bosom of civilisation. Which is why BMW began swapping the 21-inch front wheel of the original 1980 R80 GS for a smaller 19-inch hoop on 21st-century GS models. The 19-incher quickens the steering and makes riding on a winding sealed road more engaging; it’s more in line with the GS ethos than the larger front hoop fitted to dedicated off-road motorcycles. Despite the howls of some YouTubers who consider a 21-inch front to be a requisite component of an adventure bike, BMW has stuck a 19 to the new F450 GS. Chapeau, it’s a choice I applaud. This proves that BMW wanted to draw the line between the two contrary GS riding statements right down the middle with the F450 GS. This 178kg bundle of all-terrain riding fun is sampled here in the range-topping $14,490 Trophy variant that adds the snazzy paint scheme, a beefy bashplate, extra suspension adjustment, an extra riding mode targeted at extreme off-road use, and a clever auto-clutch so that the engine never flames out during a rocky river crossing. All these extras, except perhaps the motorsport-inspired paint scheme, enhance performance on the ‘Gelände’ side of the mission statement. An F450 GS Trophy, for me, almost represents the perfect balance of the two diverse design briefs. It would be even closer to perfect if the bike was equipped with some cross-spokes and 50/50 tyres instead of cast alloy wheels and 80/20 rubber biased towards road use. Be warned that such an upgrade is likely to add $2000 to the purchase price. BMW first surprised us with a ‘baby GS’ ten years ago when it released the underwhelming single-cylinder G310 GS in collaboration with its Indian manufacturing partner, TVS. The good news is that TVS and BMW have now built us a new twin-cylinder GS with what feels like twice the horsepower. If only this had been the ‘baby GS’ model that they released ten years ago. This time, BMW hasn’t held back on the new technology it’s incorporated into the new 450. There’s a new 420cc parallel twin with an innovative 135-degree crankshaft. That brings a new inline twin-cylinder engine sound into a segment where Chinese twins favour 270-degree cranks because their aural signature mimics that of V-twins and Japanese twins use 180-degree cranks because they rev more freely. It would be more accurate to call this new engine a 225-degree parallel twin. The piston of one cylinder reaches Top Dead Centre (TDC) when the crankshaft has rotated 135 degrees, while the other does the same when the crank reaches 225 degrees of rotation. Calling it a 225-degree crankshaft positions the new layout nicely between the 180-degree and 270-degree twins of the competition. This accurately describes how this lively new engine feels and sounds. It emits a more entertaining exhaust signature than a 180-degree twin and is keener to rev out than a 270-degree motor. Again, Chapeau, BMW. Next up, the ERC automatic clutch that’s standard equipment on the most expensive F450 GS, and optional on the other two variants of the range. Backed up by a rapid-fire quick-shifter for the six-speed gearbox, the ERC is a brilliant bit of kit and rivals the e-clutch system Honda now fits to the latest Transalp 750. The rpm point at which the ERC engages is set a bit higher than the Honda at 2700rpm, but you soon get used to it. Fast getaways are triggered by a quick twist of the throttle to wide open, and the F450 GS launches so sweetly that it’s hard to imagine any hand operation of the clutch lever being so devastatingly effective. Low-speed manoeuvres are a doddle and it’s easy to trickle the bike over gnarly obstacles off-road. Meanwhile, BMW retained the clutch lever on the left side of the handlebar so that a quick flick of it can initiate a wheelstand when required. The light, easy-to-ride dynamics are a highlight of the F450 GS Trophy experience.  As a Learner-Approved Motorcycle the engine is restricted, but a fully-fuelled weight that’s around 20kg less than some rival twins makes the BMW feel one of the friskier rides in the segment. There’s decent torque available in the middle of the rev range, making highway cruising feel relaxed and sustainable, along with the comfortable, if narrow, seat. At around 7000rpm, there’s an extra kick forward that’s easy to target with the quick-shifter.  Memories of the lethargic G310 GS fade to insignificance when riding the F450 GS. The engine performance is matched by that of the chassis. There’s none of the top-heaviness that blights the handling of some welterweight ADVs and it feels beautifully balanced, both front to rear and top to bottom. Capping it off are the quality suspension and brakes. The former makes the most of the modest 180mm of wheel travel, the firm springs prevent bottoming out on the big hits, and robust damping keeps the springs under control. Helped by radial caliper mounts and braided brake lines, the single front disc produces a stopping performance that’s arguably segment-leading. Want the rest of the stuff fitted to the Trophy but not the ERC, the fancy paint, nor the alloy bashplate? Buy the $13,890 Sport version of F450 GS. Sitting at the bottom of the F450 GS range is the $13,490 Exclusive, which is still a well-equipped bike by lightweight ADV standards despite the entire range lacking cruise control. For it comes with BMW’s easy-to-read 6.5-inch TFT screen and the brand’s brilliant switchgear. There’s IMU-enhanced traction control and ABS Pro, a decent selection of riding modes (minus Enduro Pro), adjustable hand levers, and a USB-C socket. Excellent ergonomic tailoring is a feature of all three models. The seat height might look a bit daunting on paper at 845mm, but in practice it’s an easy bike to swing a leg over. Buy the Sport to get arguably the most value in the new F450 GS range, but don’t sweat the decision too much. Any of these three models makes a mighty fine ‘baby GS’. $14,490  / 3.8L/100km  /  88g/km0-100 km/h 5.7sEngine  420cc  parallel twinMax power  36kW@8750rpmMax torque  43Nm@6750rpmDrivetrain Six-speed, chain driveWeight (claimed)  178kg

title: GS-JJ Enhances Custom Keychain and Pin Services for Cincinnati Businesses and Nonprofits - Cincinnati Enquirer

CINCINNATI, Ohio — November 21, 2026 — GS-JJ is enhancing its custom keychain and pin offerings, along with related design and ordering services, to support businesses, nonprofits, schools, and community groups across Greater Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky. The updates include more flexible keychain ordering options, expanded pin customization features, and design assistance to make it easier to create custom promotional products for year-end events and 2027 activities. These improvements give organizations more flexibility when selecting product styles, customizing artwork, managing order quantities, and planning production schedules. The updated offerings suit fundraisers, community events, donor recognition programs, school activities, trade shows, and other organizational gatherings. Expanded Custom Keychain Features and Ordering Options GS-JJ offers custom keychains in several materials, including soft PVC and rubber, metal, and acrylic. Each material provides different possibilities for shapes, colors, artwork, and intended uses. The updated customization options give customers more ways to develop designs around their organizations, events, and promotional goals. Custom keychains can feature different designs on each side, while metal keychains offer full-color UV layered printing for more detailed artwork and vibrant visual effects. Ordering flexibility is another important part of the offering. GS-JJ has no minimum order requirement for custom keychains, so customers can start with a single piece or choose quantities based on their needs. This option can help small businesses test a new promotional item, nonprofits preparing donor gifts, and community groups organizing events with changing attendance estimates. GS-JJ also offers a range of custom pin styles and decorative options for organizations looking to create branded, commemorative, or recognition items. Customers can choose from three common production styles: Additional customization options include rhinestones, glitter, epoxy coating, and glow-in-the-dark enamel. These features allow organizations to adapt pin designs to different themes, branding requirements, recognition programs, and special events. By offering multiple production styles and decorative finishes, GS-JJ gives customers more flexibility when developing custom pins for employees, members, donors, volunteers, and event participants. Alongside its product options, GS-JJ provides design and ordering services intended to make custom product projects easier to manage. Customers receive free artwork setup and digital proofs within 24 hours. The proof allows them to review the design before production begins, and manufacturing starts only after customer approval. Free design assistance is also available for organizations that need help preparing artwork or refining an initial concept. For repeat keychain orders, GS-JJ stores molds free of charge for two years. Customers reordering the identical design within that period do not incur an additional mold fee. This arrangement can help organizations reuse established designs for recurring fundraising campaigns, membership programs, and annual events. The AI Keychain Generator provides another way to explore product ideas. Customers can turn an initial concept into a design preview and request a quotation online. Production and Customer Support for Event Deadlines Production scheduling and delivery arrangements are important considerations for organizations preparing promotional items for specific event dates. GS-JJ publishes estimated production timelines to help customers plan their orders. Depending on the product and order specifications, metal keychains can have production turnaround times as short as two business days. Acrylic keychains typically require about 10 business days of production, followed by about 3 to 5 business days for shipping. Other custom keychain orders generally require about 10 business days of production, plus about 3 business days for shipping. These timelines are estimates, and actual schedules may vary depending on product specifications and order requirements. Customers are encouraged to confirm production and shipping arrangements before setting an event deadline. GS-JJ also lists free shipping on its keychain products. Customers can contact the company by phone, email, or live chat for assistance with product selection, artwork, quotations, and order arrangements. Supporting Cincinnati Organizations and 2027 Events Businesses and nonprofit organizations across Greater Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky have different requirements when preparing promotional products. A small business may need branded keychains for a local market, while a nonprofit may order commemorative pins for donors or volunteers. Schools, community groups, and event organizers may also need customized items for membership activities, fundraising programs, and annual gatherings. GS-JJ’s updated custom keychain and custom pins offerings, combined with flexible ordering and design support, give organizations more options for planning these projects. By considering product features, order quantities, artwork requirements, and production schedules together, customers can select items that better match their event needs and budgets. The company continues to serve organizations seeking custom promotional products for both one-off projects and recurring activities throughout the year. GS-JJ is a custom promotional products supplier serving businesses, nonprofit organizations, schools, and community groups. Its product range includes custom pins, keychains, challenge coins, medals, patches, and other personalized gifts. With a focus on quick-turn custom gifts, GS-JJ provides design assistance, digital proofs, and flexible ordering options to support organizations of all sizes and event schedules. title: Forget The BMW GS — This ADV Gives You Most Of What Matters - Top Speed
content: The big BMW GS is the undisputed leader of the full-size adventure class, dominating sales with decades of updates, massive road presence, and class-setting electronics. Buyers flock to the German flagship because it eats up cross-country miles while projecting serious status at every stop. However, that prestige carries steep initial pricing and expensive dealer service bills, putting it out of reach for riders who prioritize high-mileage dependability over badge appeal. The real question is whether you actually need to spend that kind of money for serious adventure riding. The Suzuki V-Strom 1050DE proves that you can forget the BMW GS and still get most of what actually matters for long-distance travel at a lower price. Its proven 1,037 cc V-twin engine and steel frame skip the dizzying electronic complexity of expensive European rivals, but that straightforward foundation delivers the exact substance you need out in the boondocks: great torque, predictable handling, and bulletproof mechanical longevity. By offering real cross-country competence, distinct character, and rock-solid reliability for a fraction of the cost, Suzuki skips the marketing hype entirely and gives riders everything that actually counts from the GS’s arsenal. That value-first philosophy becomes even clearer when you put its sticker price next to Munich’s flagship. The big V-Strom range starts at $15,699, but that is for the base model with alloy wheels. The 'DE' signifies its off-road intentions, and you get a spoke rim combination with tires more compatible with the dirt. This model has a base price of $16,649. There's no question that the R 1300 GS is the adventure bike benchmark, but it also asks for a lot more money for its modern features like Bluetooth, navigation, and electronic suspension, and shaft drive. The base model costs $20,395, and when you start adding options and accessories to it, you are sucked into the world of BMW's packages. It will very easily drive the price up to $25,000. In effect, the Suzuki offers most of what the BMW has to offer, but at nearly half the price. Suzuki has stuck with a V-twin engine for the V-Strom 1050DE, and this is one of the coolest examples of that engine layout. This is a 90-degree V-twin that displaces 1,037 cc, has liquid cooling, and a DOHC setup. It is a short-stroke design with a compression ratio of 11.5:1 to produce 107.4 horsepower at 8,500 RPM and 73.7 pound-feet of torque at 6,000 RPM. This V-twin does not have best-in-class power figures, but it generates most of its performance low in the rev range. For an adventure motorcycle, that is incredibly good news. The result will be lower stress and therefore better longevity and better fuel economy. It is mated to a six-speed gearbox with an assist and slipper clutch that also has hydraulic actuation. The V-Strom 1050DE chooses an old-school chassis that matches its Honda-like reliability with BMW touring comfort. This is an aluminum twin-spar frame, which is expensive to produce and heavier than the frames other adventure bikes use today, but the flip side is that the V-Strom 1050 offers some of the best feel and feedback among the competition. The suspension is provided by KYB: 43 mm inverted forks with 6.7 inches of travel and a link-type rear shock with 6.6 inches of travel. Both ends are fully adjustable. The brakes consist of twin 310 mm front discs with radial four-piston fixed Tokico calipers and a 260 mm rear disc with a Nissin single-piston caliper. These are linked brakes, which is a great feature at the price. It uses spoked rims with a 21-inch front and 17-inch rear, where you'll find one of the V-Strom's quirks: only the rear rim is tubeless. The V-Strom 1050DE is 94 inches long with a height of 59.3 inches. The seat height is 34.6 inches, and the ground clearance is 7.5 inches. It has a wheelbase of 62.8 inches, weighs 554 pounds wet, and the fuel tank can hold 5.3 gallons of fuel. These are the dimensions of a normal full-size adventure motorcycle. The seat height and ground clearance are normal for the segment, while the wheelbase is a little long for the segment, which should make it very stable at speed. That is added to by its weight. All said and done, this is a very comfortable two-up tourer that feels built for riders over 60, but don’t expect it to change direction with as much ease as the competition. The V-Strom 1050DE offers just enough features to make it an enjoyable premium experience, but it does not go overboard since V-Strom owners don't care about fancy gadgets. It leads with the five-inch TFT display, but it leaves out Bluetooth and navigation. The engine has a by-wire throttle with three ride modes, cruise control, and switchable cornering traction control. Of course, the brakes might be linked, but the rear ABS can be switched off as well. The standard equipment includes a center stand, the aluminum skid plate, the engine crash bar, and a tool-adjustable windscreen. The options list includes a taller touring windscreen, the quick-release screen adjustment kit, upper crash bars, and hard or soft luggage. We want to hear from you. title: The Outlook for Retail Stocks as Black Friday Approaches - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Analysis and forecasts on global economies and markets for the year ahead from economists and strategists across Goldman Sachs. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Solid retail sales data and a positive start to retail earnings reporting are demonstrating the strength of the US consumer heading into Black Friday, says Scott Feiler, consumer sector specialist in Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities. Low jobless claims and declining gas prices also suggest resilient consumer spending, which is showing up in sales for experiences and giving a boost to hotel and cruise-line stocks. At the same time, Feiler says on The Markets podcast that it will be important to monitor how higher material costs flow through to corporate margins and retail prices in 2027. Chris Hussey: This is The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey, and today is Thursday, November 19th. And I'm joined from our Dallas office by Scott Feiler, who is a consumer sector specialist within FICC and Equities. And this week we're going to discuss a retail sales report we got earlier in the week, what it means for the consumer, how earnings are shaping up, and what the setup into next week's Black Friday is for the entire consumer space. Chris Hussey: Okay, Scott, I was looking back at my notes. We had you on exactly a year ago. Why not? Get you right ahead of the Black Friday and also in the middle of earnings season. Back then, you were a little bit cautious on the consumer, though. Where are you falling out on the consumer in the year ahead? Scott Feiler: Yeah, I mean, you could use a couple different words. The consumer is fine. The consumer is resilient. Most of the companies that we've heard from so far sound good. Things are just steady. It's hard for me to pound the table and tell you that everyone is doing well, nor are we seeing the deceleration in the consumer that everyone expected we were going to see when gas prices were high and inflation was sticky. The consumer is fine. Obviously, you hinted the retail sales report. The October retail sales report beat again. September, last month, beat and was revised higher. So, from a top-down perspective, consumer spending is good, and from a bottoms-up perspective, the corporates generally sound steady and while that's not amazing, it's certainly a lot better than people feared a couple months ago Chris Hussey: All right. I want to talk a little bit about our strategist, Ben Sneider. He's made a very big call on consumer staples as a defensive. You're making a little bit of a call, though, talking about the consumer being strong here. Do you want to play the consumer for defense or do you want to play the consumer for offense? Scott Feiler: I mean, historically it's one or the other, right? But recently consumer discretionary and consumer staples equal weight have had a positive correlation. That's very rare. So you don't necessarily have to pick one or the other. Ben has certainly had an out of consensus call by being constructive on staples. And it's been a good call. And the group has obviously acted quite defensive as the market has gotten choppier, and if the market remains choppy, that's going to continue to work. I'm a little more constructive on consumer discretionary right now though, simply because corporates are telling us that things are fine. Jobless claims are at the recent lows, and spending is accelerating a little bit into fourth quarter, and we think Black Friday's going to be good. So, we'd be selectively constructive on consumer discretionary right now Chris Hussey: Let me explore one of those aspects of that call. You talked about gasoline prices maybe on the decline, and that is part of the inflation call here. Affordability has become a big buzzword in the economy today. How is the consumer sort of hanging in there with all the inflation they're seeing, and how are corporates that are in this space hanging in with all the inflation they're seeing? How are they keeping margins up? Scott Feiler: We got another weekly jobless claims number that was down around 200 today. So the consumer is employed and wage growth is still strong, and so they just have confidence in their job still. So, that's number one. Gas prices have come off peaks, and so the consumer has probably responded to that. Savings are still, obviously still just more elevated than most people realized, and we just haven't seen the givebacks from the tax refunds that we had earlier in this year. So, the consumer is sort of spending through those temporary inflation headwinds that we had over the last few months. And so yeah, I mean the consumer holds in. We're not in the clear yet. I do think companies still could pass on more prices. They're not fully giving the consumer back all of the tariff refunds that they've got. These corporates could continue to pass on prices into next year, though. Chris Hussey: There's also an energy lag though on that corporate side, especially in the consumer staples side, but it's also flowing through some of the retailers who deal in apparel and things like that. Are you concerned at all that you're going to see input cost inflation rise so fast that they're not going to be able to pass it on to the consumer through price? Scott Feiler: I don't think we're out of the woods yet in terms of some of the raw material costs. Even though energy prices have begun to come down, corporates are almost certainly going to have margin pressures from raw material costs next year as new contracts come up. And so there are going to be margin pressures next year. Most of the companies that we have heard from who have talked about 2027 have hinted that margins are likely to be lower next year on a year-over-year basis and below consensus. And so, we do think corporates will try to raise prices to offset some of the raw material costs that they're going to see next year on the freight side and other raw material costs. It's going to come down to who has pricing power and who doesn't. Some companies have pricing power, some companies don't. But we do think corporates are going to try and pass through prices to offset some of the raw material increases that they are going to see next year. Chris Hussey: Well, we're getting an update on that pricing power right now, cause I'm catching you right in the middle of earnings season for the retailers, maybe the heart of earnings season. What are you learning so far? Whats coming out of the earnings season that's catching your eye? Scott Feiler: Consumers are still spending on travel and experiences. The travel group is up 10% the last month. Hotel RevPAR is incredibly strong still. Everyone was expecting trends to fade after the World Cup, and they've accelerated further. Cruise lines sound really good. So, consumers are still spending on experiences and that is showing up in stock prices as well. So that's number one. And then number two is you're not seeing perfectly linear strength in trends week to week, but you are seeing the consumer remain generally resilient. The corporates we have heard from who have spoken about fourth quarter, quarter to date, the few weeks before Black Friday, have generally told us that fourth quarter has started stronger than 3Q ended. So, the consumer is still showing up and feels like it's going to be fine into Black Friday. Chris Hussey: One more question here on Black Friday, because we're going to be going into Black Friday as well here. What is your outlook for Black Friday? How much does it matter? Scott Feiler: I mean, the consumer always shows up for Black Friday or for any event for that matter. And given the consumer is employed and given sentiment has picked up off the lows in the sentiment readings, we think the consumer is going to show up next week and on Black Friday as well. They always do. November historically is very strong for the retail group. The retail group has outperformed nine of the last 10 years in a row in November, and most of that outperformance comes the last two weeks of November around Black Friday because the holiday reads we always get are generally good. And given the corporates that we've heard from over the last couple weeks have told us that things are accelerating into fourth quarter, we think that's going to continue into next week and we think retail outperformance is probably going to continue and be strong next week Chris Hussey: Yeah, it's the Cindy Lou Who economy. No matter what happens, Christmas came, Christmas came just the same. All right, good stuff. Let's put a bow on it. What's the trade? Scott Feiler: We talked on it briefly already, but I think you're supposed to buy all sorts of dips in anything travel related. Hotels, cruise lines. Hotels are going to do well. In an agentic world where people are going to book more direct through hotels as opposed to potentially through other ways, hotels do well in that world. It's a higher margin business for them. So we like hotels on any sort of pullbacks. We like cruise lines as well. Net yield growth is going to accelerate into next year. And so we like those two parts of travel. And then there's select single names that we like as well. Some discretionary names that are value, that are discounted valuations, that are quality companies that have seen real pullbacks. There's a lot of single stocks that we really like specifically that are levered to apparel, that are trading at pretty deep discounts to history. Chris Hussey: Okay, a lot coming up. What are you watching for next week and beyond? Scott Feiler: We're going to get a lot of earnings next week, over the next couple weeks. In addition to obviously we're getting Black Friday, we're going to hear from department stores and off-price companies. These are less idiosyncratic stories and more just reads on consumer health. So we're going to get those the next couple weeks. The last few weeks has been about idiosyncratic stories. The next couple weeks are going to be about consumer bellwethers and how these companies are sounding around the consumer through the first three weeks of November, and we think that's going to be incredibly important to hear from. So, next week's earnings are going to be important. Department stores and off-pricers, that's who we're watching next week, and we think it'll be generally good Chris Hussey: All right, I can't let a conversation with Dallas, go without this. Dallas Cowboys off to a tough start though, but are they going to make the playoffs anyway? Scott Feiler: I don't think so. I mean, I might get tomatoes thrown at me for saying that, but I just don't think it's going to happen unfortunately. We're just finding ways to lose games that we should win. We're just not closing it out in the fourth quarter. We're just not a fourth quarter team unfortunately Chris Hussey: Well, Scott, I appreciate that. Thank you for taking time with us this week. Chris Hussey: That does it for this week's episode of The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey. Thanks for listening. title: UNI GS Christy Hoffman to speak at Paris Summit Against International Oligarchy - UNI Global Union
content:
20.11.26 UNI General Secretary Christy Hoffman will speak at the first Paris Summit Against International Oligarchy on Saturday 21 November 2026 at the Théâtre de la Concorde. The summit was initiated by the International Tax Observatory, led by economist Gabriel Zucman. It brings together economists, researchers, politicians, journalists, trade unionists and activists to debate how to respond to extreme wealth and the concentration of economic, media and technological power. Hoffman will take part in the opening debate, “IA : pour une propriété universelle des savoirs” (AI: for universal ownership of knowledge), at 11.30 a.m. She will be joined by sociologist Isabelle Ferreras of the University of Louvain and economist Cecilia Rikap of University College London, along with a keynote address by Nobel Prize-winning economist Esther Duflo. The panel will ask who owns the knowledge that AI draws on, how the value it generates should be shared and how to stop the technology from concentrating power even further. Hoffman will argue that much of that knowledge comes from workers, whose calls and keystrokes are being recorded to train AI systems, and that they need a say in how it is used and their fair share of what it earns. “When I started work, I could not have imagined how much more power billionaires would accumulate over the following decades, and AI is now accelerating that concentration. We cannot afford a failure of imagination now, because this power is becoming more entrenched by the day. The answer must be as global as the problem, and a critical part of it is stronger unions. Workers must have real power over how companies are run, and the public must have real control over the systems we all depend on. There should be no ceiling on how just and democratic our economies can become. I’m coming to Paris to help widen what our movement believes is possible.” Other speakers at the anti-oligarchy summit include Nobel laureates Paul Krugman, Joseph Stiglitz and Duflo as well as labour leaders such as SEIU-UHW President Dave Regan and the CGT General Secretary Sophie Binet. The day’s debates draw on a manifesto signed by around 100 intellectuals and published on the eve of the summit. title: Judge orders ICE not to move Xie, a Princeton Ph.D. student and asylum seeker, out of Virginia - The Daily Princetonian
content: A federal judge ordered U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement late Friday to not remove Eva Yi Xie GS from the Eastern District of Virginia barring a further court order. The judge, Anthony Trenga ’71, also ordered ICE to respond to a petition for habeas corpus filed by Xie’s lawyers by 5 p.m. on Wednesday. Xie is a third-year Princeton neuroscience Ph.D. student who was detained by ICE at an airport in Virginia on Thursday after departing the Society for Neuroscience’s annual conference in Washington, D.C. She is being held at an ICE holding facility in Chantilly, Va. Xie, who was born in China, came to the United States in 2016 on a visa, when she was a minor. Though her original nonimmigrant status has expired, she has a pending asylum claim and an immigration court date set for early 2028, according to her lawyer, Kerry Doyle. Trenga did not immediately respond to a request for comment. ICE did not respond to multiple requests for comment on Thursday and Friday. During the current Trump administration, ICE has frequently moved detainees away from the districts in which they were detained, but Trenga’s order prohibits that from happening to Xie. Mahmoud Khalil, who was detained in New York in March 2025 as a recent Columbia University graduate, was transferred to a detention facility in Jena, La. as his case was being heard. Khalil was a prominent organizer of the pro-Palestine encampments at Columbia. Rümeysa Öztürk, a Tufts University student detained by ICE in March 2025, was also brought to Louisiana from Massachusetts. Öztürk’s student visa was revoked by the U.S. government largely due to an op-ed she co-authored in The Tufts Daily, the university’s student newspaper, that was critical of the university’s response to the Gaza war. Xie does not appear to have been outspoken on political issues at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, where she was an undergraduate student, nor at Princeton. THIS IS A BREAKING NEWS UPDATE. The Daily Princetonian’s original story follows below. Eva Yi Xie GS, a third-year Princeton neuroscience Ph.D. student who was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Virginia on Thursday, is an asylum seeker who has an immigration court date set for early 2028, her lawyer Kerry Doyle told The Daily Princetonian on Friday afternoon. A habeas corpus petition has been filed in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia by Xie’s lawyers. Xie was detained at the Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in Arlington, Va., after departing from the Society for Neuroscience annual conference, where she presented a poster on Wednesday. Rupert Li, a mathematics Ph.D. student at Stanford University who Xie is in a relationship with, told the ‘Prince’ that Xie was planning to board a domestic flight to the San Francisco International Airport to visit him. Doyle, who was arranged to represent Xie by the University, said ICE has not informed her of a reason for the arrest. ICE did not respond to multiple requests for comment on Thursday and Friday. The law office of Parastoo Golesorkhi Zahedi, based in Virginia, is also representing Xie. Doyle previously served as a principal legal adviser for ICE and as deputy general counsel of the Department of Homeland Security during the Biden administration. She is a partner at the law firm Green & Spiegel. Xie is currently being held at an ICE holding center in Chantilly, Va. She has been there since she was detained Thursday afternoon, according to Doyle. Holding centers are not fully equipped detention facilities, and they are meant to be a temporary holding location. Xie arrived in the United States from China in 2016, when she was a minor, and attended the Bronx High School of Science. She later attended the Massachusetts Institute of Technology as an undergraduate. Doyle said that Xie’s family applied for asylum within a year of arriving. The asylum claim was referred to immigration court, though Doyle said she does not yet know when that referral occurred. In the habeas corpus filing, according to Doyle, Xie’s lawyers argued that ICE detained her without a warrant. They claimed that because Xie did not have a recent change in circumstances or pose an imminent risk of leaving the country that would make a warrantless arrest necessary, Xie should be released. According to Doyle, holding facilities like the one in Chantilly don’t have accommodations like readily accessible beds and showers, making them incompatible for long-term detention. She called it “completely inhumane” to hold people at processing facilities for extended periods. In August 2026, immigration advocacy organizations reported poor conditions at the Virginia facility. The American Civil Liberties Union reported that up to 80 people were held in a single room for longer than a week without access to lawyers, medical care, or basic hygiene. Since Xie’s detention, members of the University community have advocated for her release. Princeton graduate students and Xie’s lab have called for people to send messages to politicians in New Jersey and Virginia about the case. New Jersey Senator Andy Kim’s office is directly in touch with Xie, according to Kim’s press secretary Katey Sabo. She added that his office is “working on the case” in a statement to the ‘Prince.’ Sen. Cory Booker, the other New Jersey senator, wrote in a statement to the ‘Prince’ that ICE has not responded to his outreach on Xie’s detention. Kim and Booker are both Democrats. “My office has contacted U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) regarding the detention of Eva Yi Xie and has not yet received a response. I expect a prompt and full explanation of the circumstances surrounding her detention,” Booker wrote. Wynne Stagnaro GS, a member of Xie’s lab, shared in an interview with the ‘Prince’ that Xie’s advisor, Carlos Brody, has said she is remaining calm about the situation. “‘She’s amazing, steady as a rock,’” Stagnaro said Brody wrote after speaking with Xie. “I really want Eva to be able to be back and to be able to live her life and to be able to celebrate the holiday. It’s really jarring and something that I don’t think should be happening,” Stagnaro added. İnci Çetin GS, who serves on the policy subcommittee of the Faculty Committee on the Graduate School alongside Xie, had been on a call with other graduate students right before she spoke with the ‘Prince.’ She shared in an interview that Xie has been a strong leader for the graduate student body. “She’s a really engaged person. She always brought up important issues … to the community, and she was vocal about it,” Çetin said. The Society for Neuroscience, which organized the conference Xie was attending, wrote in a statement that it was “closing monitoring the detention.” “We are in close contact with Princeton University and stand ready to provide any support that may be needed. Our thoughts are with Eva, her family, and her colleagues,” the Society added. “News of Eva’s detention is distressing for me and many members of the Princeton University community,” Dean of the Graduate School Rodney Priestley wrote in a statement to the ‘Prince.’ “We will remain in contact with her legal team, her family, and colleagues to provide support.” “We hope Eva will soon be able to resume her studies at Princeton,” Priestley added. title: Goldman Sachs (GS) Plunge 8% to Near $801 as Hot Inflation and Jobs Data Rattle Rate Outlook - FXLeaders
content: Shares of The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE: GS) tumbled sharply on Friday, plunging roughly 8% to trade near $801 per share. The drop marks the latest leg of a broader selloff that has erased nearly 30% from the Wall Street giant’s 52-week high of $1,154, pushing the stock deep into bear market territory and putting the psychological $800 threshold squarely in traders’ sights. Despite reporting record year-to-date revenue, strong third-quarter earnings, and securing lucrative lead underwriting roles on blockbuster deals—including Anthropic’s historic IPO and a $44 billion SpaceX financing package—Goldman Sachs has been caught in a perfect storm of macroeconomic headwinds and market-wide risk aversion. Broad Market & AI Rout: Wall Street is enduring its worst losing streak since 2020. A sharp pullback in artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks—compounded by regulatory concerns following the U.S. midterm elections and executive upheaval at Nvidia—has sent the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) surging above 31. As a heavyweight component of the Dow Jones Industrial Average, Goldman Sachs has been among the hardest-hit blue-chip stocks as institutional investors de-risk portfolios. Hawkish Federal Reserve Expectations: Hotter-than-expected October inflation and jobs data have forced markets to reprice interest rate expectations. With traders now anticipating potential rate hikes from the Federal Reserve by mid-2027, fears of tighter financial conditions have dampened sentiment across major banking stocks. Slowing Growth & Dealmaking Outlook: Investors are looking past Goldman’s strong 2026 earnings and pricing in a cooler 2027. Goldman Sachs’ own research team recently warned that global GDP growth in 2027 is “tilted to the downside” and projected that corporate earnings growth will decelerate significantly from 2026’s pace. A slower dealmaking and IPO pipeline directly threatens the investment banking fees that fueled Goldman’s earlier rally. Technical Breakdown: From a chart perspective, Friday’s drop pushed GS decisively below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages. Market technicians note that persistent selling pressure has broken key support levels, with some analysts eyeing the $750 to $783 zone as the next major technical floor if $800 fails to hold. On the New York Stock Exchange, Goldman Sachs—alongside Nvidia acted as the primary drag on the Dow Jones Industrial Average during Friday’s session. While value-oriented analysts point out that Goldman’s underlying fundamentals and capital-markets dominance remain intact, near-term momentum remains firmly with sellers until broader equity volatility subsides

title: Peterborough theatre history brought to life in free exhibition - Peterborough Matters
content:
David G-S as Fairy Godmother (Image: Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery) David G-S as Fairy Godmother (Image: Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery) A new exhibition is shining a spotlight on centuries of theatre history in Peterborough. Life’s a Stage, opening at Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery on 21 November 2026, explores the city’s theatrical heritage from the late 1700s to the present day. The exhibition runs until February 20, 2027, and features playbills, archive materials, and memorabilia from venues including the long-lost Theatre Royal, Hippodrome, and Embassy Theatre, as well as modern stages like The Crescent, The New Theatre, and the Key Theatre. Glenys Wass, heritage collections museum manager, said: "We are delighted to share this fascinating exhibition with our visitors. Cast of Cinderella (Image: Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery) "We have enjoyed working with current staff at Landmark Theatres and The Cresset to develop the exhibition, along with hearing memories shared by past employees to create this exhibition. "We hope people have as much fun visiting it as we did creating it." Visitors can learn about the families who managed the theatres, the performers who graced the stages, and the evolution of Peterborough’s theatrical scene. The exhibition also celebrates the city’s pantomime tradition, with props and costumes from past productions and a mini stage where guests can take part in the fun. Life's A Stage (Image: Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery) Famous names who once performed in Peterborough, including Vera Lynn, George Formby, and Laurel and Hardy—who visited in 1952—are featured in the displays. To mark the opening, the museum will be welcoming a very special guest appearance from 'The Fairy Godmother,' Dame from this year’s Cinderella pantomime at Landmark Theatre’s New Theatre, who will be joining the launch alongside one of her naughty elves. Visitors will have the chance to meet the characters and pose for photos on Saturday, November 21, between 10am and 12 noon. The exhibition is free to attend at Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery. title: Karol G's medical condition that causes weight gain: "People shouldn't care, I'm a singer" - MARCA
content: Karol G's medical condition that causes weight gain: "People shouldn't care, I'm a singer" The artist revealed it this way in her Netflix documentary titled "Tomorrow Was Very Beautiful" Singer Karol G is in one of the best moments of her professional career. Her songs and shows are a success, and projects keep multiplying in her career. One of them, without a doubt, is the appearance of her song "El Makinón" in the GTA VI video game. However, the artist has had moments in which she has not felt very well and has had health problems. Recently, she has had to postpone her concert in Mexico City due to a health issue that, according to some media outlets' speculation, could be the flu. However, in her documentary titled "Tomorrow Was Very Beautiful", she mentioned that she has another underlying health problem that "causes weight gain," an issue for which she has often been criticized, in her own words. The illness the artist suffers from, according to what she herself said, is insulin resistance, in addition to the hormonal imbalances she experiences. These two conditions work and interact in many ways but, one of them, is body weight. Insulin resistance promotes fat storage since, when cells respond poorly to insulin, the pancreas produces more to compensate. This excess, as Dr. Jorge Solano mentions, drives the body to store energy as fat and slows the use of this fuel. In addition, it is normal for those who suffer from this problem to feel an increase in hunger and cravings, due to fluctuations in glucose and insulin. On the other hand, it is normal for fat to accumulate in the abdominal and visceral area. All of this complicates weight loss and weight maintenance which, added to the hormonal imbalance, can present a fairly complex situation to deal with, especially when you have a great deal of public exposure. People shouldn't care how much weight, because I'm a singer, I'm not a model Aesthetic pressure is one of the issues women have to deal with in almost every area of their lives. One of those areas is the music industry. In that regard, many artists feel that there is a double standard when it comes to what is demanded of a man and a woman who have the same profession. Almost no man feels the scrutiny that women are subjected to in the artistic sphere. Additionally, in many cases, they feel they suffer from ageism and that natural aging penalizes women, as many women have mentioned in interviews. On the other hand, the pressure not only comes from outside, but in many cases, it is also exerted from "home". The important thing is to understand that we should not comment on other people's bodies without knowing the context, reason, or cause of a physical change. The reality is that it can have a mental health impact on the artist, which can cause anxiety and emotional strain. © 2026  Unidad Editorial Información Deportiva, S.L.U. All rights reserved. title: Chennai: Functional RWH systems now must for completion certificate - The New Indian Express
content: CHENNAI: Completion certificates for buildings in the city will be issued only after officials verify that their rainwater harvesting structures are functional, and not merely present, Greater Chennai Corporation Commissioner G S Sameeran said on Thursday. He was speaking on the sidelines of a stakeholder meeting by civic body with the Confederation of Real Estate Developers’ Associations of India (CREDAI), the Chennai Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (CMWSSB), resident welfare associations and NGOs, to promote rainwater harvesting as part of the ‘Thuli’ people’s movement. According to a CMWSSB survey of 10 lakh properties, only six lakh had functional rainwater harvesting structures. The corporation aims to raise the number to 13-14 lakh buildings, covering at least 70% of the 17 lakh assessed properties in the city, wherever feasible, particularly in larger buildings. Sameeran said a government order (G.O. 193) issued by the municipal administration and water supply department on January 2 lays down schematic diagrams and guidelines on construction of rainwater harvesting structures based on soil types. Copies of the order will be distributed to RWAs, and residents will be trained in maintaining and repairing the structures, he said. Chennai requires 1,246 million litres per day (MLD) of water, of which around 80% comes from reservoirs such as Poondi, Puzhal and Chembarambakkam, around 12% from desalination plants and around 6% from groundwater, he said. The groundwater level was recorded at 5.6 m above the aquifer in 2026 against 7.9 m during previous years of heavy rainfall, he said. Despite receiving 612 mm of rainfall against the city’s annual requirement of 850 mm, reservoir storage remains low at an average of 41% against the usual level of around 60%, and the corporation is pinning hopes on the rain between November 23 and 26 to replenish them. Asked about the poor maintenance of rainwater harvesting structures, Sameeran said the GCC had created such facilities in 1,858 buildings, 1,013 parks, 87 major playgrounds and along 30,000 stormwater drains covering 3,000 km, but some had been damaged over time. On the structures developed using German technology at the wells of the Vadapalani and Chitrakulam temples, which were later left unattended, he said there were two types of sponge parks, and the one using eco-blocks with a honeycomb-like structure may not be suitable everywhere since they are made of plastic. The corporation is also rejuvenating 245 ponds and plans to develop sponge parks using the natural gradients of the land at locations such as playgrounds. title: Princeton neuroscience Ph.D. student detained by ICE - The Daily Princetonian
content: Eva Yi Xie GS, a third-year Ph.D. student in neuroscience, has been detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement at an airport near Washington, D.C. She is believed to be held in a detention center in Chantilly, Va. Xie is the first known Princeton student to be reported to be detained by ICE. “The University has arranged for legal counsel to represent the student,” University spokesperson Michael Hotchkiss wrote in a statement to The Daily Princetonian Thursday night. The Society for Neuroscience annual conference was held in Washington, D.C., from Saturday through Wednesday. Xie presented a poster at the conference on Wednesday titled “Entorhinal grid-like coding generalizes to jointly organize physical and cognitive dimensions.” Xie is a member of the Brody Lab. She is advised by neuroscience professor Carlos Brody and coadvised by neuroscience professor Nathaniel Daw and computer science professor Benjamin Eysenbach. “It seems wildly unfair,” Brody wrote in a statement to the ‘Prince.’ “Eva is a brilliant law-abiding student and wonderful person who has many talents to contribute to the United States. Detaining her, with the intent of deporting her, makes no sense whatsoever. It is cruel, and it is our country shooting itself in the foot.” Dean of the Graduate School Rodney Priestley emailed graduate students in the Princeton Neuroscience Institute about the incident at 11:01 p.m. Thursday evening. “We hope she is able to soon resume her studies at Princeton,” the email, obtained by The Daily Princetonian, read. “Please be assured that we will stay in close contact with the student’s family, her legal team, and her PNI colleagues as this situation is resolved.” Wynne Stagnaro GS, a fellow PNI graduate student in the Brody Lab, shared specifics of the incident in a message on the Graduate Student Government Slack. According to Stagnaro, Xie sent a “call for help” to her lab mates via Slack Thursday afternoon. She told the ‘Prince’ on Friday morning that the lab mates have been able to make contact with Xie. “Eva is a brilliant computational and experimental systems neuroscientist. She is also a valued colleague, mentor, and friend, and we are privileged that she chose our lab for her thesis research,” Stagnaro wrote in her message. “She went to a conference to present her work, and now she’s in a detention center. She should be home.” An X post from the Brody Lab shared similar sentiments. Stagnaro shared that members of the Brody Lab have been in touch with the office of Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., other elected officials, and members of the media. Stagnaro did not add anything beyond the Slack post in a statement to the ‘Prince.’ Xie is researching the “neural basis of decision-making.” She emigrated from China to the U.S. in 2016. She graduated from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 2024 with double majors in computer science and mathematics and a concentration in economics. She has interned with Meta, Microsoft AI, and IBM Research, among others. At MIT, Xie was one of three undergraduates elected to the Presidential Advisory Cabinet for Institute President Sally Kornbluth and chaired the MIT Judicial Review Board. She is now on the Policy Subcommittee of the Princeton Graduate Student Committee on the Graduate School. Xie previously organized a workshop called “Data on the Brain & Mind” for the 2025 Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems. She is currently co-organizing the Annual Conference on Cognitive Computational Neuroscience for 2027 in Edinburgh, Scotland. Eysenbach and Daw could not immediately be reached for comment. ICE did not respond to multiple requests for comment. A correction was made Nov. 21, 2026: A previous version of the photo credit on this story misspelled the photographer’s name. She is Louisa Gheorghita, not Lousia. The ‘Prince’ regrets this error. title: US Stocks Are Predicted to Extend Their Historic Rally as Gains Moderate - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Analysis and forecasts on global economies and markets for the year ahead from economists and strategists across Goldman Sachs. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. The S&P 500 has generated triple-digit returns since the start of the bull market four years ago. While US stocks are forecast to climb higher in 2027, Goldman Sachs Research expects US stock returns to moderate as earnings growth slows. What is Goldman Sachs Research’s outlook for S&P 500 gains in 2027? The S&P 500 is predicted to generate a total return of 18% through the end of 2027 (as of November 17), writes Ben Snider, chief US equity strategist, in the team’s report. Earnings are expected to grow by a robust 11% in 2027, or 18% excluding mega-cap tech “other income” from private investment stakes. However, that is a step down from the roughly 30% growth rate this year, and growth will likely slow further in 2028. “Positive but decelerating growth has historically been associated with positive but moderating S&P 500 returns as well as rotations within the equity market,” Snider writes. In these environments, returns are typically driven by earnings growth as valuation multiples decline. US stocks are on pace in 2026 for a fourth-straight year of gains, and the S&P 500 has returned 120% since late 2022. This four-year bull market return ranks as the strongest in the last 50 years outside of the dot-com bubble and the recoveries following recessions, according to Goldman Sachs Research. “AI investment has driven a surge in S&P 500 earnings in 2026, but that tailwind should begin to fade in 2027,” Snider writes. Capital expenditures in artificial intelligence (AI) have produced about half of the S&P 500’s growth in earnings per share this year. That impulse will likely be smaller in 2027 as the growth rate of capex slows and depreciation expenses build, according to Goldman Sachs Research. Earnings growth is also expected to slow modestly in 2027 for companies outside of AI infrastructure. Even so, Snider expects earnings, rather than valuations, to continue to drive equity returns in 2027. He says elevated interest rates, decelerating earnings growth, and AI-driven uncertainty should prevent broad expansion in multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E) ratios, in 2027. “The biggest downside risk to equities in 2027 is a deterioration in the earnings outlook for 2028,” Snider writes. AI investment growth will likely remain robust in 2027, as will its contribution to S&P 500 earnings. However, the market is forward looking, and that theme could play out in a broad range of ways in 2028. In addition to uncertainty around AI investment spending in 2028, the potential for rising semiconductor supply threatens profit margins and earnings, according to Goldman Sachs Research. Our strategists estimate that each $50 billion of AI capex, or 1 percentage point change in semiconductor profit margins, in 2028 would shift S&P 500 earnings-per-share (EPS) growth by about 1 percentage point. If consensus S&P 500 EPS estimates fell back to the 30-year trend and the P/E ratio fell to the 30-year average of 17x, the S&P 500 would decline by roughly 25% to a level of approximately 5,600. In addition, S&P earnings growth and recent stock returns have been highly concentrated in a handful of stocks. As the earnings growth from the AI investment cycle fades, the key question is whether another sufficiently large source of earnings strength will emerge to sustain index-level profits, Snider writes. Some of the dynamics during the late stages of other bull markets—such as Federal Reserve rate hikes—are taking place today. “One striking contrast with past overextended bull markets is the lack of speculative mania in today’s market,” Snider notes. He points out that recent equity returns have generally tracked near-term earnings outlooks. While active fund managers faced a difficult backdrop in much of 2026, Snider says earnings-driven returns, elevated dispersion, and improving equity market breadth bode well for stock pickers heading into the new year. What themes are expected to drive US stocks in 2027? As AI capex decelerates, Snider expects investors to shift their focus to “the next earnings beneficiaries of the AI boom.” For example, cloud-operating hyperscalers have increasingly shown signs of monetization of their AI investments. Another theme in 2027 may reflect the surge in corporate borrowing that has taken place to fund AI investment. Strong capex has come in part at the expense of buybacks, according to Goldman Sachs Research. That may create opportunities in “buyback aristocrats”—stocks with strong free cash flow generation and a commitment to returning cash to shareholders. During the past few decades, periods of slowing earnings and economic growth have favored stocks with price momentum, upward earnings revisions, and "quality" attributes such as low volatility and strong balance sheets, Snider writes. He says the information technology and healthcare sectors have a history of outperformance in these situations. Investors may also benefit from diversifying into defensive stocks, such as consumer staples companies, that tend to deliver stable profits even when the economy slows, according to Snider. “Although our base case is for continued earnings growth and equity market appreciation, the downside risks associated with extended earnings and valuations argue for diversifying portfolios with select defensives,” he writes. title: GS Caltex Overcomes Delay, Secures Sole Lead - 조선일보
content: 20-Minute Halt for Emergency Patient; GS Caltex Wins 3-1, Tops Standings [OSEN=Cho Hyung-rae Reporter] The match was delayed for about 20 minutes due to an emergency patient during the game, leading to a chaotic continuation. GS Caltex defeated Heungkuk Life Insurance. GS Caltex won 3-1 (25-19, 25-20, 18-25, 25-23) in the ‘2026-2027 HK Financial Group V-League Women’s Division’ match against Heungkuk Life Insurance held at the Incheon Samsan World Gymnasium on the 19th. With this victory, GS Caltex extended its winning streak to three games, recording 4 wins, 1 loss, and 12 points. It tied with the Industrial Bank of Korea (IBK) and Korea Expressway Corporation on points (4 wins, 1 loss each) but took sole first place by leading in set ratio. Heungkuk Life Insurance suffered its third consecutive loss, with 6 points (2 wins, 3 losses). GS Caltex dominated the first and second sets. In the first set, trailing 12-13, Tana scored two points from serves, and Silva successfully scored consecutive open attacks. Combined with Heungkuk Life Insurance’s touch net error, GS Caltex reversed the momentum to lead 18-13. The second set was also tightly contested, but with the score tied 17-17, Kwon Min-ji scored a blocking point. Heungkuk Life Insurance’s touch net error, Kim Hyo-im’s serve point, and Silva’s open attack gave GS Caltex the upper hand. However, an unexpected situation occurred in the third set. Heungkuk Life Insurance took control early. Leading 5-4, Jastis’s quick open attack, Jung Ho-young’s block, followed by Jung Ho-young’s quick spike and serve points, extended the lead to 9-5. Kindelan, Jastis, and Jung Ho-young’s points, along with Kindelan’s serve point, helped Heungkuk Life Insurance fend off GS Caltex’s comeback. Then, with Heungkuk Life Insurance leading 19-14 in the third set, an emergency patient occurred in the first-floor spectator area near the main office. The match was immediately halted, and on-site medical staff were deployed. After about 20 minutes of emergency treatment, including the arrival of 119 paramedics, the patient was transported to the hospital. The match resumed at 8:43 p.m., and Heungkuk Life Insurance won the third set. In the fourth set, GS Caltex overturned the tight battle. Yu Seo-yeon’s open attack tied the score at 22-23, followed by Kim Hyo-im’s serve point to reach 24-23 and secure the match point. Oh Se-yeon’s open attack completed the victory. GS Caltex had four players score double digits: Gisele Silva with 22 points, Choi Ga-eun with 12, Tana with 12, and Kwon Min-ji with 11. Heungkuk Life Insurance’s Kindelan scored 35 points, and Jung Ho-young added 14, but they failed to stop the losing streak at home. /jhrae@osen.co.kr

Benelli and GS Motos have taken another step forward in their industrial strategy in Mexico with the start of production of the Benelli TNT25N at GS Motos’ manufacturing plant in Toluca. The model joins the Benelli 180S and TNT150, which began production in July, further strengthening the brand’s presence within GS Motos’ local manufacturing operations. The launch follows the introduction of models from Hero Motos, Benelli, and Morbidelli in 2026. With operations in Toluca and Guadalajara, GS Motos is strengthening its multi-brand manufacturing strategy and expanding its production capabilities in the Mexican market. “For GS Motos, assembling the Benelli TNT25N in Mexico means much more than simply bringing production closer to the market. It means combining the experience and discipline of local teams with a motorcycle that retains the brand’s sporty character and Italian inspiration. This new assembly operation reflects our confidence in GS Motos’ manufacturing capabilities and in the talent that makes each unit possible,” said Jorge García Puente, Director of Global Operations at GS Motos. The TNT25N production line operates at a rate of 34 units per hour, equivalent to approximately one motorcycle every 1.8 minutes. This pace is supported by a synchronized production process involving personnel, standardized procedures, and quality controls, with each station ensuring the precision and quality required for continuous production. The GS Motos manufacturing plant in Toluca has an annual production capacity of 1.2 million motorcycles. Since beginning operations in 2008, the facility has manufactured more than 10 million units. The start of TNT25N assembly further strengthens the role of the Toluca facility as a strategic manufacturing hub for GS Motos in Latin America. With the addition of the TNT25N, GS Motos is expanding its assembly capabilities in Mexico by incorporating another model into its multi-brand manufacturing operations. The move highlights the flexibility of its infrastructure and the expertise of its teams in producing motorcycles from different brands according to specific standards and requirements. The model’s integration into Mexican production lines also supports the development of skilled talent by combining Italian-inspired motorcycle design with the technical expertise of GS Motos’ local workforce. title: BREAKING: BMW R 12 G/S Launched In India: Meet The New Retro Scrambler - ZigWheels.com
content: BMW Motorrad has launched the BMW R 12 G/S, launched in India. It is priced at Rs 25,40,000 (ex-showroom). The bike gets a proper retro look. The design of the motorcycle is inspired by the legendary BMW R 80 G/S, which was the foundation of the modern GS bikes, and has won 4 Dakar Rally titles. Nonetheless, the R 12 G/S looks mesmerising from any angle you look. The bike gets an 'x'-shaped DRL, which hints at how riders used to tape their headlights to hold broken glass together during a race crash. The bike gets proper purposeful bits, which elevates its look even more. The handguards look sleek, and they should protect your brake and clutch levers when you have a fall. The tank caves out a bit where you place your knee. This should give you more leverage and surface to grip while riding the bike offroad, where the situation requires you to stand up and ride. Also, the left-side mounted exhaust is cherry-on-top, which makes the bike look like how those classic enduro bikes look. The bike gets a semi-digital console that features an analog speedometer and a digital insert which shows the odometer, gear position indicator and the ride modes. The bike gets 3 riding modes: Rain, Road and Enduro. These modes change how the bike responds to input according to the mode selected. Also, the bike gets cornering ABS and traction control, making the bike safer. The bike is powered by a 1,170 cc air/oil-cooled, twin-cylinder boxer engine. The motor makes 109 PS at 7,000 rpm and 115 Nm at 6,500 rpm and is paired to a 6-speed gearbox. Also, it has a claimed top speed of 210 kmph. The bike is suspended on a fully-adjustable 45 mm upside-down fork with 210 mm of travel. Rear is taken care of by a fully adjustable monoshock unit with 200 mm of travel. Also, it gets a Paralever swingarm, and the bike gets a shaft drive setup. It rolls on a 21-inch tubeless cross-spoke wheel upfront and gets a 18-inch wheel at the rear. Braking duties are handled by twin 310 mm discs upfront and a single 265 mm disc at the rear. The bike gets a tall saddle height of 875 mm, and it gets a 15.5-litre fuel tank. Also, the bike weighs 229 kg (kerb). The BMW R 12 G/S is a premium retro-styled roadster. What makes it unique is its air and oil-cooled boxer engine that not only looks cool, but might also help with its handling. That said, it has no natural rivals as such in India. The Triumph Scrambler 1200 X is comparable in terms of performance but it costs almost half of the German bike. If you are looking for a retro-looking motorcycle with a heritage, the R 12 G/S makes perfect sense. Thanks for reporting this. title: BMW R 12 G/S off-roader launched at Rs 25.40 lakh - Autocar India
content: BMW’s 1,170cc boxer-twin engine is somewhat of a legend, thanks largely to the R 1200 GS and the GS Adventure. However, not many remember that it only received liquid cooling in 2013, before which it was an air- and oil-cooled mill. If you are one of the few who happen to remember it and miss it, you now have the choice to buy the R 12 G/S, which BMW calls a heritage enduro off-roader. Of course, in keeping with the times, the motorcycle juxtaposes its classic styling with notable modern upgrades. As we said, the R 12 G/S is powered by a 1,170cc, air- and oil-cooled boxer-twin engine making 109hp at 7,000rpm and 115Nm at 6,500rpm. This engine is also shared with the R 12 nine T and R 12, although the latter gets a slightly lower state of tune (95hp at 6,500rpm and 110Nm at 6,000rpm). The R 12 G/S also shares the dry clutch with its heritage cousins, as well as the tubular space chassis, but with major changes considering its positioning as a serious off-roader. BMW has given it a 45mm USD fork with 210mm travel, along with full adjustability; the G/S even shares the fully adjustable paralever swinging arm rear suspension but with 200mm travel. As is expected of a motorcycle with off-road pedigree, it runs on a 21-inch front and 18-inch rear wheel setup, with the convenience of tubeless cross-spoke rims. The said wheels are stopped by dual 310mm front discs with axially mounted 2-piston calipers and a 265mm rear disc with a 2-piston caliper. Of course, dual-channel and cornering-sensitive ABS is standard. Because of such focused changes, the kerb weight has gone up to 229kg, the wheelbase is 1,580mm, and the seat height is a towering 875mm. Combined, these make the R 12 G/S the heaviest, longest and tallest heritage motorcycle yet from the German manufacturer. However, the road-oriented R 12 nine T gets a half-litre larger fuel tank than the G/S’s 15.5-litre unit. Despite the motorcycle being an unmissable throwback to the legendary R 80 G/S – down to the now phased-out G/S branding – BMW has been generous with the amount of rider aids on offer. There are four ride modes, namely Rain, Road, Enduro and Enduro Pro, the last being available with the standard Enduro package that also adds the aforementioned 18-inch rear wheel, enduro footrest, handlebar risers, hand lever protector and a large engine guard. The riser adds a 20mm lift to the G/S’s handlebar. There’s a standard Comfort package too, which adds a bi-directional quickshifter, cruise control, hill-start assist and heated grips. Of course, there’s lean-sensitive traction control and a BMW-specialty drag torque control as well. All these systems work via the on-board computer, as the R 12 G/S sticks to an analogue instrument cluster with a tiny digital display at the bottom. While the lighting is all-LED and BMW has afforded features such as an immobiliser and a keyless system to the motorcycle, it sticks to a 12V socket to charge your devices. Internationally, BMW offers three colours, but India gets only one: Light White in a single Pro variant. The BMW R 12 G/S is priced at Rs 25.40 lakh (introductory), and deliveries have commenced. At its price point, it sits between the R 1300 GS (Rs 24 lakh) and R 1300 GS Adventure (Rs 26.50 lakh).

title: BMW R 12 G/S Price Starts At Rs 25.40 Lakh In India - RushLane
content: BMW R 12 G/S is on sale in India at an introductory Rs 25,40,000 ex-showroom. BMW Motorrad imports it as a Completely Built-Up (CBU) motorcycle. India receives the Pro variant.  Configurea BMW R 12 G/S draws design cues from BMW R 80 G/S, which entered production in 1980. BMW links the model to its off-road sport history, boxer engine and shaft drive. This concept spans more than four decades. Design details include enduro styling, long suspension travel, cross-spoke wheels and a compact cockpit fairing. A high-mounted rear silencer sits on the left-side exhaust system.  Configurea BMW Power comes from a 1,170 cc air/oil-cooled boxer engine. It produces 109 hp, or 80 kW, at 7,000 rpm. Peak torque is 115 Nm at 6,500 rpm. Bore and stroke measure 101 mm and 73 mm. BMW traces its boxer heritage to the R 32, launched in 1923. A one-piece tubular bridge steel spaceframe forms the chassis. Tubular steel main and rear sections form the frame. The rear section bolts to the main frame. Steering head sits higher and further forward. Two rear steel eyelets serve as lashing points. The butted aluminium handlebar allows ergonomic adjustment. Suspension uses a fully adjustable 45 mm upside-down front fork with 210 mm travel. A Paralever swinging arm works with an angled rear spring strut. Rear travel measures 200 mm. The front wheel measures 21 inches. The Enduro Package adds an 18-inch rear cross-spoke wheel and off-road tyres. BMW lists the Enduro Package as standard, with eight additional equipment options. Items include the 18-inch rear wheel, off-road tyres, enduro footrests, engine guard and 20 mm handlebar risers. Enduro Pro riding mode is included. Footrests and risers support a standing riding position off-road. Standard Comfort Package includes Shift Assistant Pro, adaptive Headlight Pro, Hill Start Control, Cruise Control and heated grips. Shift Assistant Pro enables clutchless gear changes across almost all load and speed ranges. It reduces shift times and limits power interruption during acceleration. Lighting uses an LED headlight with X-shaped light icons. Braking uses twin 310 mm front discs and a single 265 mm rear disc. Both ends have two-piston floating calipers. ABS Pro is standard, with part-integral operation and cornering assistance. Riding modes comprise Rain, Road and Enduro. Enduro Pro comes with the Enduro Package. DTC and MSR are standard; riders can switch DTC off for off-road use. BMW provides a three-year warranty. Extended coverage is available for years four and five. Road-Side Assistance operates 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, offering breakdown support and towing. Optional equipment and BMW Motorcycle accessories are available. Hardeep Singh Brar, President and CEO, BMW Group India said, “The new BMW R 12 G/S brings an icon back to its roots. Inspired by the legendary BMW R 80 G/S, it combines authentic enduro character with modern technology and the unmistakable spirit of the BMW boxer. Purist, purposeful and built for adventure, the BMW R 12 G/S is for riders who find their greatest experiences beyond the familiar. We are thrilled to launch the BMW R 12 G/S in India, inviting enthusiasts to explore more, ride further and create their own adventures.” Started in 2008, RushLane is India's leading auto news website. title: BMW R 12 G/S Launched at Rs. 25.40 Lakh - BikeWale
content: BMW Motorrad has launched the gorgeous new R 12 G/S in India at Rs. 25.40 lakh (ex-showroom). This retro-styled adventure motorcycle draws inspiration from the venerable R 80 G/S of 1980. It combines a 1,170cc boxer-twin with long-travel suspension, cross-spoke wheels and dedicated off-road equipment. It is available exclusively in the Pro variant for India with both the Comfort and Enduro packages included as standard. However, its 229kg unladen weight and 875mm seat height suggest that it will demand considerable experience when the going gets difficult. Drawing inspiration from the legendary R 80 G/S that established the foundations of the manufacturer's modern adventure motorcycle range, the new R 12 G/S features a high-mounted front mudguard, compact cockpit fairing, relatively slim fuel tank and a flat seat. Its exposed boxer engine and high-mounted exhaust further contribute to its traditional enduro appearance. The R 12 G/S concentrates on simplicity and a more purposeful design which makes soo desirable. For India, BMW is offering the motorcycle in a single Light White paint scheme complemented by a contrasting red seat and traditional graphics, like the original R 80 G/S. Its compact LED headlamp features BMW's distinctive X-shaped lighting signature and the relatively minimal bodywork keeps the motorcycle's mechanical components clearly visible. A centrally positioned circular instrument display reinforces the retro character. The 1,170cc air- and oil-cooled boxer-twin engine puts out 109bhp at 7,000rpm and 115Nm of torque at 6,500rpm. It comes with shaft final drive. BMW has developed a dedicated chassis arrangement for its off-road use. It features a tubular steel frame with a repositioned steering head and the rear subframe is bolted to the main structure. Front suspension has fully adjustable 45mm upside-down forks offering 210mm of wheel travel. Rear uses its Paralever swingarm with a fully adjustable monoshock offering 200mm of travel. The R 12 G/S uses a 21-inch front cross-spoke wheel. Enduro Package, included as standard in India, adds an 18-inch rear wheel with off-road tyres. Package also brings enduro footpegs, a larger engine guard, hand protection, a longer side stand and handlebar risers. The latter raise the handlebar by 20mm, improving the ergonomics when riding while standing on the footpegs. It weighs 229kg unladen and the seat height stands at 875mm in its Indian spec. The R 12 G/S also features a 15.5-litre fuel tank. India-spec R 12 G/S additionally receives the Comfort Package as standard. This includes Shift Assistant Pro for clutchless gear changes, heated grips, cruise control, Hill Start Control and adaptive headlight functionality through Headlight Pro. BMW is importing the R 12 G/S to India as a completely built-up unit, with deliveries commencing immediately. The motorcycle also comes with a 3-year/unlimited-kilometre warranty that can be extended into the fourth and fifth years.

title: Medicine Pricing: Patients Deserve Transparency, Not Just an MRP – Gs Gopal Raaj. - City Today News
content:
News media, Ayurveda, Healthcare,Sidha medicine,Technology,Electronics, Food, Travel, Social Media, etc The wide gap between the actual manufacturing cost of medicines and their printed Maximum Retail Price (MRP) raises serious questions about transparency and accountability in India’s pharmaceutical industry.If a medicine costs just ₹10 to manufacture but carries an MRP of ₹100, what justifies the tenfold difference? Patients have every right to know how the prices of medicines, particularly essential and life-saving drugs, are determined.While pharmaceutical companies have legitimate expenses, including research, clinical trials, regulatory compliance, distribution and business operations, these factors should not become a reason for excessive pricing or unreasonable profit margins.The government must consider stronger transparency measures, including appropriate disclosure of medicine pricing structures and closer monitoring of pharmaceutical profit margins. Patients should not be left in the dark about the pricing of medicines on which their lives depend. Healthcare is not merely a commercial business. It is a service closely connected with human life, dignity and survival. Pharmaceutical companies deserve reasonable returns for their investments and innovations, but social responsibility must remain equally important.A life-saving medicine should not become a financial burden for the very people who depend on it to survive. The time has come for the pharmaceutical industry and policymakers to put patient welfare at the centre of medicine pricing.– G.S.
